summary: James Irving Manatt was a scholar of history, archaeology, and linguistics. He studied at Grinnell College and Yale under William Dwight Whitney, holding posts at Denison, Marietta, the University of Nebraska-Lincoln, the United States, and Brown University (1892–1915).

James Ishmael Ford is a religious and Buddhist studies scholar and Zen founder. He studied at Sonoma State and Pacific School of Religion, and trained under Mel Weitsman, Jiyu-Kennett, and John Tarrant. He taught Josh Bartok.

James Kennedy worked in Indology, history, and archaeology. He studied at the University of Edinburgh, served as a missionary with the London Missionary Society until 1877, lectured at University College London, and was treasurer of the Royal Asiatic Society (1904–1919).

James Kenneth Powell II is a Buddhist studies scholar. He studied at Northwestern University, the University of Chicago under David Tracy, and the University of Wisconsin-Madison under Geshe Lhundup Sopa, Isshi Yamada, and David M. Knipe.

James L. Fitzgerald specializes in Indology and religious studies. Educated at the University of Chicago under Edwin Gerow, J. A. B. van Buitenen, and Edward Byles Cowell, he held posts at the University of Tennessee, Knoxville and Brown University.

James L. Taylor is a scholar of religious and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD from Macquarie University in 1989 and was attested as Senior Lecturer in Anthropology at the University of Adelaide in 2014.

James Legge was a sinologist who studied at the University of Aberdeen and Highbury College. He served with the London Missionary Society, the Anglo-Chinese College, and Oxford University as Professor and Fellow of Corpus Christi College from 1876 to 1897.
James Liddell Phillips worked in linguistics and religious studies. He was educated at Whitestown Seminary, Bowdoin College, and the Columbia University Vagelos College of Physicians and Surgeons.
James Long was an Indologist and linguist. He studied at the Church Missionary Society College, Islington in 1838, and served as a missionary for the Church Mission Society starting in 1840.
James Low is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Edinburgh and received traditional training under Chhimed Rigdzin Rinpoche.

James Luther Adams was a scholar of religious studies and philosophy. He studied at the University of Minnesota Twin Cities, Harvard Divinity School, and Harvard University, where he also held a post from around 1957 to 1968.

James M. Macphail was an Indology and linguistics scholar. He earned an M.A. and M.D. from the University of Glasgow, founded the Bamdah Medical Mission in 1890, and served as a physician with the Free Church of Scotland (1889–1929).

James Mackintosh worked in history, Indology, and philosophy. Educated at Aberdeen and Edinburgh, he founded and presided over the Asiatic Society of Mumbai and served as Professor of Law and General Politics at East India Company College (1818–1824).

James Macnabb Campbell was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. Educated at The Glasgow Academy and the University of Glasgow, he served in the Indian Civil Service from around 1869 to 1897.

James Mallinson is an Indologist who studied at SOAS and the University of Oxford under Alexis Sanderson. He held posts at Balliol College, SOAS, and Wolfson College, becoming Oxford's Boden Professor of Sanskrit in 2023.

James Mark Shields is a scholar of religious studies, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. He has held appointments at Bucknell University (2007–2010, 2017) and the International Research Center for Japanese Studies (attested 2016).
James Matthew Baskind is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Japanology. He completed his PhD at Yale University under the supervision of Stanley Weinstein.

James McHugh is an Indology and religious studies scholar educated at Cambridge, Oxford, and Harvard. He was an Assistant Professor of Religion at the University of Southern California (attested 2009–2012) and held a post at Cornell University.

James Miller is a sinologist and religious studies scholar. He studied at the University of Cambridge and Boston University, and served as Professor of Chinese Studies and Religious Studies at Queen's University Belfast (attested 2014).

James Morison was an Indologist educated at Oxford and the University of Vienna under Georg Bühler and Arthur Anthony Macdonell. He served as Librarian at the Indian Institute, University of Oxford, in 1914.
